patch_description: Prior generations showed that collapsing the trainable-parameter set to just 2 unique values (either two global RY/RZ angles, or two group angles reused across RY/RZ) already reaches perfect train/val/test accuracy (score 0.72, n_params=14). The 4-unique-parameter variant only hurt score (0.66) despite identical accuracy, confirming the score is dominated by parameter economy once accuracy saturates. This version pushes economy further: a single scalar angle "theta" drives every RY gate in the pre-entanglement layer and every RZ gate in the post-entanglement layer (reused, not separate), combined with a lightweight open nearest-neighbor CZ chain (no wrap-around) for entanglement, which previously gave the fastest convergence (30 steps) and lowest depth (29) among equally-accurate designs. This yields only 1 trainable parameter per block repetition (n_params expected ≈ 8, versus 14 for the previous best), maximizing parameter_efficiency while keeping the same expressive single-qubit-rotation + linear-entangler backbone that already reliably reaches 100% accuracy with near-zero generalization gap.
